idea: Companies ranked staff by how much AI they burn, and people burned AI to climb. Whatever you count, people learn to produce.
flow: Cold open: Hanoi, 1902, a cent a rat tail, so people farmed rats.
The mandates: Shopify, Duolingo, Microsoft and Coinbase judge staff on AI use.
The leaderboards: Meta's Token Legend and Cache Wizard, Amazon's KiroRank, agents left running to climb them.
The U-turns: Meta drops token counts from reviews; Amazon calls the metrics deeply flawed.
The proof: one company halved its AI target and sales rose 7%.
The punchline: the famous cobra story about this never happened.
ending: If you're counting how much AI your people use, you're counting rat tails.
takeaway: 3 things you can do tomorrow: scrap any target or ranking for AI use; make "AI didn't help here" a good answer; judge AI on a number you already track.
angle: Funny and investigative: the AI boom ran a century-old mistake in 18 months.
tone: Playful, with real receipts; his face shares the screen with the leaderboard, the rats and the chart.
